_about: The voice pass (2026-11): every character's candidate voices, for tools/voice-pilot.py. Each style is a Voice Studio 'Describe a voice' description in three parts: who they are, how the voice sounds, how they speak. sample: what each designed candidate says (the clip every game line is later cloned from), written in the character's usual manner. pitch (Hz, median) and rate (words a second): what a candidate should roughly land on. lines: the moments the test lines are taken from (the first clip of that moment, from the packs in 'packs' order). calm: the model is given the line with full stops for '!' and lower case for ALL CAPS (captions keep the script's words). Wording rules from the earlier voice tests: no loud, booming, brash, shouting or barking (the model shouts, far too high, and distorts); no rasp or gravel (comes out as distortion); say low-pitched, deep, steadily. An accent goes first and plainly ('heavy Texas accent'). Voices are designed from words only, never cloned from a real person.

styles.describe: A timid, gentle office worker in his thirties. A light, quiet, hesitant voice. Worried and careful, starting sentences and second-guessing them. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Flustered
styles.describe: A flustered, well-meaning man in his thirties who worries about everything. A light, quick tenor voice. Jumpy and apologetic, trying hard to stay calm. Clear studio recording.

inferno.name: Inferno
inferno.sample: They call me Inferno. Last week I ate a pepper so hot it filed a complaint. Give me your hottest. Then make it hotter.

styles.label: Intense
styles.describe: A hot-sauce fanatic in his forties, proud and intense. A low-pitched, deep, steady voice. Slow-burning and dramatic, like a wrestler making a promise. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Action hero
styles.describe: A tough, proud man in his forties who talks like an action-movie hero. A deep, low, steady voice. Serious and intense about small things. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Proud boaster
styles.describe: A proud, boastful daredevil in his forties. A deep, strong, warm voice. Confident and fiery, bragging happily. Clear studio recording.

rita.name: Rita
rita.sample: Hey there. I've been pouring concrete since five this morning. I'll take one of everything, and then we'll talk about lunch.

styles.label: Hearty
styles.describe: A strong, cheerful construction worker in her forties. A full, warm, sturdy voice, medium-low for a woman. Hearty and good-humored, always ready to eat. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: The foreman
styles.describe: A confident woman in her forties who runs a building site. A clear, strong, practical voice. Direct and friendly, with a big appetite and a big laugh. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Easygoing
styles.describe: A big-hearted, easygoing woman in her forties in a hard hat. A warm, round, relaxed voice. Jolly and plain-spoken. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Irish builder
styles.describe: Heavy Irish accent. A cheerful construction worker in her forties. A full, warm, sturdy woman's voice. Hearty and good-humored, always hungry. Clear studio recording.

lulu.name: Little Lulu
lulu.brief: Big dramatic sighs, then very sure of herself (seven years old)
lulu.sample: Hmm. Chocolate. No. Strawberry. No. This is the hardest day of my whole life. Okay. I know. Vanilla.

styles.label: Dramatic little girl
styles.describe: A seven-year-old girl, small and very dramatic. A high, bright, little girl's voice. Agonising over every choice, then suddenly completely certain. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Small and bossy
styles.describe: A bossy, confident seven-year-old girl. A high, clear child's voice. Serious and decisive, like a tiny queen. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Sweet and thoughtful
styles.describe: A sweet, thoughtful seven-year-old girl. A soft, high, young child's voice. Slow and careful, thinking out loud. Clear studio recording.

walt.name: Grandpa Walt
walt.brief: Cheerful and nostalgic, a little slow
walt.sample: Well, hello there! In nineteen fifty-five, a sundae cost a nickel, and you got a handshake with it. Those were the days.

styles.label: Jolly grandpa
styles.describe: A cheerful elderly grandfather around eighty in a letterman jacket. A warm, aged, slightly creaky old man's voice. Jolly and nostalgic, taking his time. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Old-time radio
styles.describe: A sprightly old man around eighty who sounds like a nineteen-fifties radio announcer. A bright, friendly, old-fashioned voice. Chipper and sentimental, a little slow. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Gentle storyteller
styles.describe: A kind, elderly man around eighty who loves to tell stories. A soft, warm, aged voice. Slow, fond and contented. Clear studio recording.

pa.name: Announcer
pa.sample: Attention, food court guests. A new restaurant is now open. Please walk, do not run, to the grand opening.

styles.label: Bright (woman)
styles.describe: A professional shopping-mall announcer, a woman in her thirties. A smooth, bright, pleasant voice. Calm, clear and friendly, evenly paced. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Smooth (man)
styles.describe: A professional public-address announcer, a man in his forties. A smooth, warm, polished voice. Calm, clear and reassuring, evenly paced. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Cheery (woman)
styles.describe: A cheerful department-store announcer, a woman in her forties. A warm, sing-song, pleasant voice. Upbeat and clear, like good news over the speakers. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: London announcer
styles.describe: London accent. A professional food-court announcer, a woman in her thirties. A smooth, bright, pleasant voice. Calm, clear and friendly, evenly paced. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Bright (more seeds)
styles.describe: A professional shopping-mall announcer, a woman in her thirties. A smooth, bright, pleasant voice. Calm, clear and friendly, evenly paced. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Bright and warm
styles.describe: A professional shopping-mall announcer, a woman in her thirties. A smooth, bright, warm voice. Friendly and clear, with a gentle smile, evenly paced. Clear studio recording.

styles.label: Bright and crisp
styles.describe: A professional public-address announcer, a woman in her thirties. A crisp, bright, pleasant voice. Clear and polished, evenly paced, every word distinct. Clear studio recording.

_round2_about: Round 2 (2026-11-11), after Bryan's pilot notes: shorter descriptions that lead with the defining trait (the accent study found long trait lists come out wrong), six seeds a style. identity: a short description added to a line's delivery for the '+ description' takes, to test whether a cloned voice keeps its qualities on every line. respell_ing: the model gets -ing for -in' (dropped g's read as Southern). no_tags: sound tags are left out for the model.
_round3_about: Round 3 (2026-11-11), after round 2: Bev picked (round 2 brisk-s6). Briefs in the order voice-design guides recommend (accent first, then age and gender, persona, then the sound itself); 'elderly' and Midwestern for Marge (Bryan); 'a man's voice' for Vernon (two round-2 takes came out female); Sal tries eye-dialect spellings in his sample (cawfee, tawk) to pull the New York vowels. No identity takes (round 2: '+ changes the delivery, not consistently better or worse').
_round4_about: Round 4 (2026-11-11): the round-3 descriptions made with Qwen3-TTS (tools/voice-qwen.py) instead of VoxCPM2, so the two models are compared on identical briefs. Qwen's cloning takes no delivery note.
_round5_about: Round 5 (2026-11-11): cloner A/B test, VoxCPM2 vs Qwen3-TTS Base, on picked voices (voice-pilot.py clonetest).
_round6_about: Round 6 (2026-11-11): cloner test 2: VoxCPM2 then Seed-VC (pitch model) vs VoxCPM2 vs Qwen3-TTS (voice-pilot.py vctest).
_round7_about: Round 7 (2026-11-12): cloner test 3: Chatterbox Turbo (delivery tags) vs VoxCPM2 vs Qwen3-TTS (voice-pilot.py cbtest).
_round9_about: Round 9 (2026-11-12): the other sixteen, briefs reworded with the pilot lessons (accents from the known-good list only, no rough-texture words, "elderly/aged" for age, one extra accent style for variety on four). Designed with VoxCPM2.
_round10_about: Round 10 (2026-11-12): the same sixteen briefs as round 9, designed with Qwen3-TTS (tools/voice-qwen.py), so each character can come from whichever model gets it.
_round11_about: Round 11 (2026-11-12), after the stress test: Vernon, Bev and Kai redone for VoxCPM2, picked on expression. Candidates come from (a) "retakes": VoxCPM2 cloning the current pick saying the sample, three seeds with a delivery note and three without, so the reference is VoxCPM-native and as clean as the best take (Vernon's Qwen voice drifted under VoxCPM); (b) new designs; (c) earlier runners-up never tried on expressive lines. Every kept candidate then says five expressive lines the way the game makes them (two takes, the better kept), next to the current pick.
_round12_about: Round 12 (2026-11-13), after Bryan's round 9/10 picks: the expressive-line test (as round 11) for the voices still undecided. Reginald, Brock: round 9 picks + retakes (consistency). Oakes: round 9 lecturer-s2 vs round 10 Qwen lecturer-s3 cloned by VoxCPM. Breeze: round 10 Qwen mellow-s3 + retakes vs new SoCal/hippie designs. Priya (Indian), Hiro (Japanese, untested accent): accent-led designs. PA: variations on round 9 'bright', heard through a speaker effect on the page. The other nine keep their round 9 picks.
_round13_about: Round 13 (2026-11-13): accent-only round for Priya (Indian) and Hiro (Japanese) after round 12 missed. Wordings built on the Sphere Splash accent test (Assets/tools/voice README, round A3: 'with an Indian English accent. Natural and authentic, not exaggerated.' nailed Indian; Japanese 'close'), accent at the end, shorter character text, place-of-origin and second-language phrasings. Sample line only, rated on 'accent came through'; winners then get the expressive-line test.
_round14_about: Round 14 (2026-11-13): Priya's accent found in round 13 (Bryan: C delhi-s6, D chennai-s5, E delhi-s4 good accents, clarity needs work; picked E). Clarity: VoxCPM retakes of all three (a clone keeps its clip's accent) + more seeds of the place wordings; then the five expressive lines.
_round15_about: Round 15 (2026-11-13): Hiro WITHOUT an accent (no Japanese in VoxCPM's reach; GLOBE has no Japanese data for a LoRA). Round 13's takes all distorted, so: the cleanest round 9 designs, retakes of the clearest (master-s2, clarity 4.23), more master seeds, and a 'steady' wording without 'low/deep' (the low end distorts); keep-range 100-150 Hz; then the expressive lines.
